## Character Replacement with Build Scene Prompts

This workflow uses Build Scene Prompts to assemble detailed positive and negative prompts from reusable scene and character JSON files.

Image 01 provides the pose and composition. Image 02 and later images provide character designs.

Select a scene, specify the character reference directory, and assign characters to slots A, B, and C. The node loads their reference images and inserts their features into the prompt template.

## Reference Image Roles

Image 01 — Rough Pose / Composition Reference

Image 01 defines:

- Pose and ground contact
- Composition and framing
- Camera angle and perspective
- Character placement
- Depth, spacing, and overlap

Load this image separately and connect it to the generation workflow as the first reference image. Build Scene Prompts does not load Image 01.

Image 02 and Later — Character Design References

These images define each character’s face, hair, coloring, identifying features, and reference clothing.

Build Scene Prompts loads them from the selected character folders. Connect the occupied image outputs after Image 01, in numerical order.

## Node Inputs

| Input | Purpose |
|---|---|
| scene | Select a scene JSON from the installed package’s presets/scenes/ directory |
| character_root | Parent directory containing character folders; leave empty to use examples/character-references/ |
| character_a | Character folder name assigned to scene position A |
| character_b | Character folder name assigned to scene position B |
| character_c | Character folder name assigned to scene position C |
| scene_overrides | Optional JSON text that overrides selected scene settings for this execution |

Example:

scene          = courtyard.json
character_root = D:\CharacterReferences
character_a    = character_01
character_b    = character_02
character_c    = None
scene_overrides = {}

Paths refer to the computer running ComfyUI. Character inputs contain folder names relative to character_root.

At least one character must be specified. Empty character inputs or None disable that slot. Selecting the same character folder more than once produces an error.

## Character Files

Each character folder contains a reference image and a Build Scene-specific character.json.

CharacterReferences/
├── character_01/
│   ├── image.png
│   └── character.json
└── character_02/
    ├── character.png
    └── character.json

The image field specifies the reference image filename relative to its character folder.

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "image": "image.png",
  "fields": {
    "name": "Character 01",
    "hair_spec": "Long black hair reaching mid-back",
    "eye_color": "Brown eyes",
    "facial_marks": "A small beauty mark below the character's own LEFT eye",
    "hair_silhouette": "Long straight hair",
    "age_and_context": "Preserve the apparent age from the reference",
    "fixed_features": "Preserve the reference face, hairstyle, colors and outfit construction",
    "accessory_specs": "Do not invent additional accessories",
    "failure_modes": "Wrong hair color, missing beauty mark, mirrored beauty mark"
  }
}

name, hair_spec, eye_color, and fixed_features are required.

The existing TXT-based loaders remain separate. Build Scene Prompts does not read or update positive.txt and negative.txt; those files may remain alongside character.json.

## Scene Files

Scene JSON files are stored in:

comfyui-character-scene-package/
└── presets/
    └── scenes/
        ├── reference-layout.json
        └── courtyard.json

A scene contains global settings under values and position-specific settings under slots.

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "name": "Courtyard",
  "values": {
    "environment_description": "A quiet courtyard with a stone path",
    "lighting": "Soft daylight",
    "background_treatment": "Slightly blurred distant trees"
  },
  "slots": {
    "a": {
      "position": "front-right, nearest camera",
      "pose": "Standing with both feet on the ground, matching Image 01",
      "gaze": "looking toward the camera",
      "expression": "A relaxed smile"
    },
    "b": {
      "position": "back-left, further from the camera",
      "pose": "Sitting on a bench, matching Image 01",
      "gaze": "looking toward the camera",
      "expression": "A gentle smile"
    }
  }
}

Scene slots support:

- position
- pose
- gaze
- expression
- unique_details
- nearby_props
- omitted_features

Character identity comes from character.json. Position, pose, expression, and gaze come from the scene. Replacing a character therefore preserves the scene’s instructions for that slot.

See presets/scenes/README.md for the complete field reference.

## Slot and Image Assignment

A, B, and C identify scene positions. Image numbers are assigned consecutively to occupied slots.

| Occupied slots | Reference assignment |
|---|---|
| A only | A → Image 02 |
| A and B | A → Image 02, B → Image 03 |
| A and C | A → Image 02, C → Image 03 |
| A, B, and C | A → Image 02, B → Image 03, C → Image 04 |

When B is disabled, C keeps the position and pose defined in slots.c. It does not become Character B.

Unused slots are omitted from the generated prompts. Their unused image outputs contain 1×1 black placeholders; do not connect those outputs to the image encoder.

Unlike the existing Multi Prompt Package Loader, Build Scene preserves the selected scene-slot letters.

## Prompt Structure

The node produces positive and negative prompts using three sections:

- COMMON — Style, reference-image roles, composition constraints, and shared rules
- SCENE — Environment, lighting, camera, position, pose, gaze, and interactions
- CHARACTER — Assigned character features and character-specific failure cases

Output order:

COMMON → SCENE → CHARACTER

The detailed template retains its composition-locking and identity-mapping instructions. JSON settings supply the variable content.

## Temporary Scene Overrides

Use scene_overrides to change individual settings without editing the saved scene file.

{
  "values": {
    "lighting": "Warm evening light"
  },
  "slots": {
    "a": {
      "expression": "A cheerful smile"
    }
  }
}

Priority:

Template defaults → Scene JSON → scene_overrides

Overrides merge by field. Changing A’s expression leaves its saved position and pose intact.

This input accepts multiline text and can also receive a STRING connection from another node. It does not write changes back to the JSON file.

## Node Outputs

| Output | Purpose |
|---|---|
| positive_prompt | Assembled positive prompt |
| negative_prompt | Assembled negative prompt |
| diagnostics | Assembly warnings or OK |
| image_02–image_04 | Selected character reference images |
| character_count | Number of selected reference characters |
| character_mapping | Scene-slot, image-number, character-name, and folder correspondence |

Inspect the final prompts and character_mapping before generating.

## Workflow Connections

Load Image: rough reference ───────→ Image 01

Build Scene: image_02 ─────────────→ Image 02
Build Scene: image_03, if occupied → Image 03
Build Scene: image_04, if occupied → Image 04

Build Scene: positive_prompt ─────→ Positive prompt input
Build Scene: negative_prompt ─────→ Negative prompt input

Image/text encoding → Sampling → VAE decoding → Preview / Save

Use image viewers to inspect the rough and character references. Connect text previews to the prompt, mapping, and diagnostic outputs when checking settings.

## Notes

- The current template supports one to three reference characters.
- Total people default to the selected character count. If the scene includes additional people, specify n_total, category_breakdown, and secondary_character_group_spec.
- Scene values and slot values must be strings, including n_total, such as "3". schema_version is the integer 1.
- Omitted fields use defaults. Empty strings omit the template line containing that field, which may also contain other fields.
- Input text is inserted literally. Placeholder expressions inside JSON values are not expanded again.
- New scene filenames may require restarting ComfyUI and refreshing the interface. Changes to selected JSON files and reference images are read on the next execution.
- The node assembles prompts; it does not verify that the generated image follows every instruction.
